mainTopic: רבי יוחנן explains that his earlier ruling follows רבי יוסי, who holds that the holiness of ארץ ישראל from the second entry never ended, so תרומה nowadays is דאורייתא. The גמרא then challenges רבי יוחנן's view on mixtures in rabbinic matters, using a case of a מקוה.
overview: רבי יוחנן explains that his ruling about a כהן who is an אנדרוגינוס follows רבי יוסי. A ברייתא from סדר עולם, which רבי יוחנן says was taught by רבי יוסי, shows that the second holiness of ארץ ישראל never ended, so תרומה nowadays is still דאורייתא. Next the גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן really holds that a rabbinic mixture needs no majority, citing his comment 'until most of it' on a מקוה. Two answers follow. First, 'until most of it' may mean only that most must not be removed, so an equal mix is still fine. Second, the baskets case is different because we can reason 'שאני אומר'. The גמרא then tests רבי יוחנן's view that an אנדרוגינוס is a full male. It first works through the משנה's words 'נושא' and 'אבל לא נישא'. It then turns to רבי אליעזר's ruling on stoning, concluding that both opinions treat him as a male and argue only about stoning in two places. The amud ends as רב begins a new statement, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says his ruling follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers the earlier challenge by saying his ruling follows the view of רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I said what I said according to רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge against his earlier ruling. He explains that he ruled according to the opinion of רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that רבי יוחנן's ruling about a כהן who is an אנדרוגינוס seemed to clash with treating תרומה nowadays as only דרבנן. רבי יוחנן answers that he is following רבי יוסי, who holds that תרומה is still דאורייתא today. The next steps prove that this is really רבי יוסי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: But I (רבי יוחנן speaking about himself)
what I said
according to the view of רבי יוסי

phrases.english: But I said it according to Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is talking about his own earlier ruling, the one that was just challenged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier challenge, from before this section, against רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ruling to a specific תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked as if רבי יוחנן's ruling did not fit the common view that תרומה nowadays is only דרבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן follows רבי יוסי, for whom תרומה nowadays is still דאורייתא.

steps.title: סדר עולם: the second inheritance of the land lasts forever
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in סדר עולם reads the פסוק as teaching that there was a first and a second inheritance of ארץ ישראל, but there will be no third.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in סדר עולם: 'that your fathers inherited, and you shall inherit it.' They have a first and a second inheritance, but they do not have a third.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show what רבי יוסי holds. It quotes a ברייתא from the book סדר עולם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses 'inherit' twice: 'your fathers inherited' and 'you shall inherit.' So there were two times the land was made holy: once in the days of יהושע and once in the days of עזרא. 'No third' means the second holiness never ends, so the מצוות of the land, like תרומה, still apply דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: An early book of Jewish history and dates
the first inheritance (entering the land with יהושע)
the second inheritance (returning with עזרא)
third

steps.confusionAlert: 'They do not have a third' does not mean the land loses its holiness. It means the opposite: the second holiness is permanent, so a third one will never be needed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the view that the holiness from the time of עזרא lasts forever. That view affects whether land-based מצוות are דאורייתא today.

phrases.english: As it was taught in Seder Olam:
"That your fathers inherited, and you shall inherit it"
a first and a second inheritance, they have;
but a third, they do not have.
phrases.notes: In other words, the second holiness stays forever, so a third one will never be needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the view that רבי יוחנן says he follows.
steps.raayaObject: That there is an opinion that the holiness of the land, and so תרומה, continues דאורייתא today.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא in סדר עולם explaining דברים 30:5

steps.title: רבי יוסי is the author of סדר עולם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן identifies רבי יוסי as the תנא of סדר עולם, which connects the ברייתא to רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Who taught סדר עולם? רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof by showing that the ברייתא from סדר עולם is the opinion of רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא alone does not say whose view it is. רבי יוחנן's known statement that סדר עולם was taught by רבי יוסי closes the loop. So 'I follow רבי יוסי' means 'I follow the view that the land's holiness, and תרומה, is still דאורייתא.'

keyTerms.meaning: Who taught (who is the author of this teaching)?

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's ruling follows רבי יוסי, the author of סדר עולם. רבי יוסי holds that the second holiness of ארץ ישראל never ended, so תרומה nowadays is דאורייתא.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן תְּנָא סֵדֶר עוֹלָם — רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: Who taught Seder Olam? Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the ברייתא from the last step, which completes the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the view in סדר עולם belongs to רבי יוסי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement: 'מאן תנא סדר עולם – רבי יוסי'

steps.title: Challenge: does רבי יוחנן not need a majority in rabbinic matters?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי יוחנן's view that rabbinic mixtures need no majority. It cites a משנה about a מקוה where רבי יוחנן limits the rule to 'until most of it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוחנן really hold that in a rabbinic matter we do not need a majority? But we learned: a מקוה that has exactly forty סאה, and someone added a סאה and took out a סאה, it is still kosher. And רבי יהודה בר שילא said in the name of רבי אסי in the name of רבי יוחנן: this works only until most of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against רבי יוחנן. It asks whether he really holds that in a rabbinic matter we do not need the permitted part to be the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that drawn water makes a מקוה unfit is only דרבנן. Still, רבי יוחנן says the trick of adding and removing one סאה works only until most of the original water is gone. That shows he does require a majority even in a rabbinic matter, which seems to contradict what was said in his name.

keyTerms.meaning: in a matter that is only rabbinic law
a majority, or a larger amount of the permitted part
a ritual bath
forty סאה, the minimum amount of water for a kosher מקוה
exactly, with nothing extra
until most of it

steps.confusionAlert: 'עד רובו' does not mean the מקוה becomes unfit right away. It means you can keep adding and removing one סאה at a time only until most of the original kosher water has been replaced.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yochanan hold
that in a rabbinic matter we do not need a majority?
phrases.notes: The permitted part doesn't have to outnumber the forbidden part in order to cancel it out.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: מִקְוֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה מְכֻוּוֹנוֹת,
phrases.english: A ritual bath that has exactly forty se'a,
if one added a se'a and removed a se'a, it is fit.
phrases.notes: The added סאה is drawn water or another liquid that would not count toward a מקוה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda bar Sheila said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Until most of it.
phrases.notes: After that point the original kosher water is no longer the majority, so the rule stops working.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בִּדְרַבָּנַן לָא בָּעֵינַן רִבּוּיָא? וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the source for רבי יוסי's view to a new attack on another view held by רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view held by רבי יוחנן that in rabbinic matters a majority is not needed to cancel out a forbidden mixture.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Drawn water in a מקוה is only a rabbinic problem, yet רבי יוחנן limits the add-one, remove-one rule to 'until most of it.' So he does require a majority in a rabbinic matter, which contradicts the view attributed to him.

steps.title: Reading 'until most of it' as 'most must remain'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presses its challenge. It says רבי יוחנן's limit must mean that most of the original kosher water has to remain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't this mean that most of it must remain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it started in step 4. It explains how it reads רבי יוחנן's words 'until most of it'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If most of the original kosher water must remain, then the kosher part must be the majority. That would show that even a mixture forbidden only by the רבנן needs a majority to cancel the forbidden part. This goes against רבי יוחנן's ruling that no majority is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Doesn't it mean...?' A way of offering a reading that the גמרא is about to test
Remains, is left over
Most of it, its majority

phrases.english: What, is it not that its greater part must remain!
phrases.notes: 'Its greater part' means most of the original kosher water in the מקוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge by spelling out how the cited ruling should be read
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that a mixture forbidden only by the רבנן needs no majority
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Until most of it' means a kosher majority must remain, so a majority is needed even for rules of the רבנן

steps.title: No, it only means most must not be removed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that reading. The rule only says that most of the water must not be taken out, so an equal mix is still fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means that most of it must not have been taken out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge by reading 'until most of it' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem only begins once most of the original water is removed. If exactly half remains, the kosher water is not a majority, yet the מקוה is still fine. So this case does not prove that a majority is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: No. Used to reject the suggested reading
Is taken out, removed

phrases.english: No, it means that its greater part must not be removed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by rejecting its reading
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the מקוה ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Until most of it' can mean 'until most is removed', which still allows an equal mix

steps.title: A second answer: the case of 'שאני אומר' is different
steps.stepSummary: Another answer is offered. רבי יוחנן's lenient ruling is about a case where we can say 'שאני אומר', so a majority is not needed there for a special reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say: here is different, because we can say 'For I say...'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, separate way to defend רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if a majority is usually needed for rules of the רבנן, the two-baskets case is special. We can assume the תרומה fell into the תרומה basket and the regular food fell into the regular basket. Because of that reasoning, no majority is needed there.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say...' Introduces a second answer
Here is different
'For I say...' The reasoning that lets us assume the permitted outcome happened

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer narrows רבי יוחנן's leniency to cases where we can reason 'שאני אומר'. It is not a general rule that rabbinic mixtures never need a majority.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
It is different here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' points back to the case of the two baskets, one with תרומה and one with regular food.

phrases.english: since it is possible to say 'For I say.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the step 4 challenge, separate from steps 5 and 6
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's ruling seemed to mean that no rabbinic mixture ever needs a majority
steps.terutzMaskana: The leniency comes from the 'שאני אומר' reasoning in the baskets case

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה 'אנדרוגינוס נושא'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new challenge. The משנה says an אנדרוגינוס marries a woman, which sounds like it is allowed from the start, as if he is a full male.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: an אנדרוגינוס marries a woman!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It challenges with a משנה that seems to treat an אנדרוגינוס as a complete male.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'נושא' sound like he may marry a woman even at the start. If so, he is fully a male. Then a כהן who is an אנדרוגינוס should let his wife eat from holy food, which goes against the view that he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with both male and female body parts
Marries (a woman); takes a wife

phrases.english: We learned: A hermaphrodite marries a woman!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts to a new challenge about the status of an אנדרוגינוס
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that an אנדרוגינוס is not treated as a full male
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'נושא' implies he may marry from the start, so he must be a full male

steps.title: Read it as 'if he married'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה should be read 'אם נשא'. It is talking about after he already married.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as: if he married.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by adjusting how the משנה should be read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the משנה only says that a marriage he already made counts after the fact. It no longer shows that he may marry from the start, so it does not prove he is a full male.

keyTerms.meaning: If he married (after the fact)

phrases.english: Teach: 'If he married.'

steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'נושא' means he may marry from the start
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means 'if he married': the marriage counts after the fact

steps.title: But the משנה says 'נושא'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה's actual word is 'נושא', which sounds like it is allowed from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 9, because the words of the משנה do not seem to fit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing 'נושא' into 'אם נשא' looks forced. The plain wording still suggests he may marry from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, doesn't it...?
It teaches, it states

phrases.english: But it teaches 'marries'!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's actual word 'נושא' sounds like it is allowed from the start

steps.title: Prove it from 'אבל לא נישא'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the next clause, 'אבל לא נישא', must be about after the fact. So 'נושא' is also about after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning, what does 'but he is not married to a man' mean? Rather, what does 'married' mean? After the fact. So 'marries' is also after the fact!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its answer by comparing the two halves of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'he may not be married to a man' only makes sense as a rule about after the fact: such a marriage does not take effect. Since that clause is about after the fact, the matching clause 'נושא' is also about after the fact. So it does not mean he may marry a woman from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning, a way of turning the question back on the one asking
Is married (to a man), is taken as a wife
After the fact, once it already happened

steps.whatToRemember: This is only a temporary defense. In the next step the גמרא rejects it with 'אמרי, לא': 'נושא' can still mean the marriage is allowed from the start.
steps.confusionAlert: 'נושא' (he marries a woman) and 'נישא' (he is married to a man) look almost the same. They point in opposite directions, so read the vowels carefully.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning: what is 'but he is not married'?
phrases.notes: 'Not married' means not married to a man. This is the next part of the same משנה.

phrases.english: Rather, what does 'married' refer to? After the fact,
so 'marries' is also after the fact!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 and supports the reading of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparing the two halves of the same משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'נושא' means he may marry from the start
steps.terutzMaskana: Like 'לא נישא', the word 'נושא' describes what happens after the fact

steps.title: The two clauses can be read differently, so the proof falls away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer from Step 11. 'נושא' can mean allowed from the start, while 'אבל לא נישא' means not valid even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: No. 'He marries' means from the start. 'But he is not married' means not even after the fact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 11. It shows that the two clauses of the משנה do not have to be read the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 argued that since 'אבל לא נישא' must be about after the fact, 'נושא' must be too. Here the גמרא says no: 'נושא' really does mean he may marry a woman from the start, and 'לא נישא' means that if he married a man, it does not count even after the fact. So the challenge from Step 10 is back in place.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start; allowed to be done in the first place
After the fact; once it was already done
Is married (is taken as a wife), here meaning to a man

phrases.english: They say: No.
"He marries" means from the start,
"But he is not married" means not even after the fact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 11 and brings back the challenge of Step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the סיפא that 'נושא' must be about after the fact.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two clauses can be read differently. 'לא נישא' means not even after the fact, so it does not force 'נושא' to mean only after the fact.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's words suggest the first תנא is unsure
steps.stepSummary: From the סיפא, where רבי אליעזר says one is stoned for an אנדרוגינוס like for a male, it seems the תנא קמא is unsure whether he is a male.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the סיפא teaches that רבי אליעזר says one is liable to stoning for an אנדרוגינוס as for a male, this shows that the first תנא is in doubt about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge from the end of the משנה. It aims at the view that an אנדרוגינוס is clearly a male.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says one is stoned for relations with an אנדרוגינוס, just as with a male. If רבי אליעזר needs to say this, it seems the תנא קמא disagrees and treats the אנדרוגינוס as a doubt. That would go against the view that he is a definite male.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of the משנה
Death by stoning
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
By implication; it follows that
He is in doubt about it

phrases.english: But since the last clause teaches,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
For an androgynos, one is liable to stoning as for a male,
it follows that the first tanna
is in doubt about it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge from the end of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that an אנדרוגינוס is clearly a male (רבי יוחנן).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי אליעזר must say an אנדרוגינוס is like a male, it implies the תנא קמא disagrees and is unsure about it.

steps.title: Both agree he is a male; they argue about stoning in two places
steps.stepSummary: Both the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר agree an אנדרוגינוס is a male. They only argue whether one is stoned for relations in two places or only in one place, as with a male.
steps.simpleTranslation: For both this Sage and that Sage it is obvious. The difference between them is stoning for two places. One Sage holds one is stoned for him in two places, and the other holds only as for a male.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows that the dispute in the משנה is not about whether the אנדרוגינוס is a male at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions treat the אנדרוגינוס as a male. The תנא קמא says one is stoned for relations with him in either of two places. רבי אליעזר says one is stoned only for the place one would be stoned for with any male. So the משנה gives no proof that the תנא קמא is in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Both for this Sage and for that Sage
It is clear and obvious to him
The difference between them is
From two places

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the תנא קמא is in doubt about the אנדרוגינוס. He treats him as a male and actually goes further than רבי אליעזר: one is stoned for relations in two places, not just one.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר both treat an אנדרוגינוס as a male. Their only dispute is whether stoning applies in two places or one.

phrases.english: Both for this Sage and for that Sage
it is obvious,
phrases.notes: It is obvious to both of them that an אנדרוגינוס counts as a male.

phrases.english: the difference between them is
stoning for two places.
phrases.notes: He has both male and female parts, so relations can happen in two places of the body.

phrases.english: For one Sage holds:
one is liable to stoning for him from two places,
and the other Sage holds: as for a male.
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר: stoning only for the place one is stoned for with any male.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין לְמָר בֵּין לְמָר מִפְשָׁט פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the point of the dispute in the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר argue over whether an אנדרוגינוס is a male at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree he is a male. They argue only whether stoning applies in two places or only in one.

steps.title: רב begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new statement in the name of רב. The statement itself comes next.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It introduces a statement of רב, and his words come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only tells us who is speaking. The content of רב's statement continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rav said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. This line only introduces רב's coming statement.
